issue.notes:
Implementation landed in commit 2a8891b (master, pushed to Forgejo origin).

FINDING — the gap was real but different from the spike's premise. Mechanism existed since ba9dcef and was correctly wired (every _select_track auto path returns kind='asr', manual paths '', _do_fetch forwards kind to parse_json3 at fetch.py:377); the spike (ytt-80dd25ec) itself was already closed 'in source'. But dedup keyed on WINDOW COVERAGE (emit only if tStartMs >= last_end_ms), modeling the classic re-emit shape. I captured a real YouTube ASR json3 track live (dQw4w9WgXcQ en asr, yt-dlp, 2026-09-24): modern tracks roll caption WINDOWS — consecutive content events overlap in time (dDurationMs overhangs next tStartMs) while carrying DISJOINT text, with empty erase events and a leading no-segs event. issue.description:
Add instrumented HTTP-client tests proving OIDC discovery, JWKS, token exchange, and Whisper transcription POSTs never use YTT_PROXY_URL, including failure paths. Separately verify direct-first and ip_blocked-only proxy retry behavior for YouTube captions and audio downloads.

issue.notes:
Implemented the negative half of the YTT_PROXY_URL contract as a new instrumented suite, tests/unit/test_proxy_isolation.py (13 tests, all passing). Instrumentation point: every httpx.AsyncClient.__init__ under a test is recorded (authlib's upstream OAuth client subclasses it, so it is captured too), plus fastmcp's discovery httpx.get; the sentinel proxy is configured via YTT_PROXY_URL in every test with HTTP(S)_PROXY/ALL_PROXY stripped, so any leak into construction kwargs fails the suite.

Legs: (1) OIDC discovery — success (exactly one proxy-free fetch of the configured config_url) and failure (ConnectError fails startup after exactly one attempt, never a proxied retry). (2) Token exchange + transparent upstream refresh — success drives the full e2e grant and asserts 2 proxy-free upstream dials (code exchange + refresh; fastmcp refreshes upstream unconditionally, verified in fastmcp source); failure (IdP 400) surfaces at /auth/callback because this fastmcp exchanges eagerly there, with exactly one upstream attempt and the client-facing grant dead. (3) JWKS pinned at its strongest level: verifier is symmetric-local (HS256, client secret), jwks_uri None, so valid-token verification and expired-token rejection construct ZERO clients — a proxied fetch cannot exist. (4) Whisper ASR POST through the production client run_whisper_job builds itself (no injected client): success + HTTP 500 + ConnectError + ReadTimeout all land asr_failed with exactly one dial and one proxy-free client construction; startup model guard pinned likewise (success + fail-open on ConnectError, no retry). (5) Static AST leg: ytt/ never writes the proxy into the process environment (trust_env vector).

Repairs over attempt 1 (which died mid-stream): import fixed (harness fixture is 'client', not 'asgi_client' — re-exported via a local fixture), stream-death garbage in the token-exchange test replaced with monkeypatch-fixture arming, fastmcp attribute fix (provider._token_validator, not .token_verifier — verified in pinned fastmcp 3.4.x source), MockTransport responses now carry their request for raise_for_status, and the failure-path test restructured for the eager-at-callback exchange. The bead's separately-verify leg (direct-first + ip_blocked-only proxied retry for captions and audio downloads) is pinned by the committed tests/unit/test_proxy.py and was run green here (exit 0). ruff clean on the new module. docs/notes/proxy-egress.md now records where both halves of the traffic table are pinned. issue.description:
Extend OAuth conformance coverage for JWKS key rotation, expired or not-yet-valid tokens, wrong issuer or audience, invalid signatures, and discovery/JWKS outages. Document whether validation fails closed or uses cached keys and how operators recover.

---
Priority: P1
Created by: weave strand
issue.notes:
Specified and tested OIDC key rotation + token-validation failures; found and fixed two fail-open temporal gaps.

WHAT EXISTS: ytt federates to Authentik via FastMCP OIDCProxy; the reference IdP signs HS256 keyed by the client secret and publishes an EMPTY JWKS, so ytt builds its own symmetric verifier (the JWKS default would fail closed on every token). OAuthProxy re-validates the stored upstream id_token on EVERY request (proxy.py load_access_token step 3), and validation is fully offline (static keys from settings; discovery fetched eagerly once at construction).

FINDINGS (verified empirically against fastmcp 3.4.2, pinned source): FastMCP JWTVerifier checks exp only-if-present and never nbf -> a signed id_token with exp stripped verified OK (immortal session), and nbf one hour in the future verified OK. Both bite only on validly-signed tokens (IdP-misbehavior hole, not caller-facing). All signature/iss/aud failure modes already fail closed.

FIX: ytt/auth.py UpstreamIdTokenVerifier(JWTVerifier) - exp mandatory (OIDC Core sec 2), nbf honored with 60s leeway (RFC 7519 4.1.5); wired into build_auth_provider.

NEW COVERAGE (tests/unit/test_oauth_conformance.py, 6 classes / 23 tests): invalid signatures (attacker key, tampered payload, alg=none, malformed -> None not raise); temporal claims (missing exp rejected, nbf leeway boundary); upstream secret rotation (old-secret tokens die at redeploy, no dual-key window); ytt-issued token rotation (signing key HKDF-derives from the client secret by default so ONE rotation logs everyone out - pinned; issued tokens carry exp, never nbf); JWKS path fail-closed (empty JWKS/outage/unknown kid reject; cached keys serve through outages max 1h TTL, pinned 3600s; rotated-out kid dies at TTL expiry); discovery outage (construction-time fetch failure prevents startup - fail closed; post-startup validation structurally offline).

DOCS: docs/notes/auth.md section 'Key rotation and token-validation failures' - two key families table, offline/no-cache property, failure-mode table, operator runbook (rotate via single shared OpenBao path secret/ardenone-cluster/ytt/oauth + declarative-config rollout, never live kubectl; YTT_JWT_SIGNING_SECRET as the decoupling/global-logout lever; IdP outage postures at startup vs mid-run).

NOTE for reviewers: the shared working tree currently fails test_canary_once.py collection - that is another worker's uncommitted ytt/canary.py refactor (import of _probe_one renamed), NOT this bead; all verification here ran in a clean git archive extraction of HEAD.

Not adopted because: plan.md gates it to an explicit human choice that hasn't been made; no agent-reachable Cloudflare token can read/edit zone WAF rulesets (pjp-815ae8ba credential blocker); the zone-wide http_request_firewall_custom phase ownership risks clobbering unverifiable dashboard rules on a shared zone (the hazard that retired the legacy terraform/cloudflare root); and the drifting Anthropic egress range makes an unattended edge block a standing availability liability. issue.description:
Decision record for the gap on ytt-11881410: docs/notes/auth.md named inbound IP-allowlisting of Anthropic's MCP egress (160.79.104.0/21, 2607:6bc0::/48) as Cloudflare Access/WAF defense-in-depth, with no bead authoring or declining it.

DECISION: deliberately NOT adopted for now. The subject allowlist + audience-bound OAuth (fail-closed, YTT_ALLOWED_SUBJECTS, DCR off) is the real per-tool authz and stands on its own without an edge IP rule — docs/plan/plan.md §"Inbound IP allowlist": 'defense-in-depth only ... stands on its own if the host-level WAF is skipped'. The plan also gates this to a human choice ('the host-level Cloudflare WAF rule only if explicitly chosen') and no operator has chosen it.

Corrections to the premise, for whoever revisits:
- Access is wrong for this use (plan §86): Cloudflare Access is an identity gate that would challenge/bounce Anthropic's unattended backend. Only a WAF custom rule fits.
- Path-scoping IS expressible, so the do-no-harm constraint is satisfiable at the rule level. ytt's live public path space (k8s/ardenone-cluster/ytt/ingressroute.yml) is /ytt plus three /.well-known/*/ytt metadata paths, so: (http.host eq "mcp.ardenone.com" and (starts_with(http.request.uri.path, "/ytt") or ends_with(http.request.uri.path, "/ytt")) and not ip.src in {160.79.104.0/21 2607:6bc0::/48}) with action=block leaves every /ibkr path untouched. Validate the mixed v4/v6 'in' set against the ruleset engine at adoption time — no token here can test it.

Why declined now (each independently sufficient):
1. Optional per plan; human-gated; not chosen. P3 defense-in-depth behind an already-live fail-closed subject allowlist (ytt deployed, well-known endpoints 200 on mcp.ardenone.com as of 2026-09-16).
2. Credential blocker: no agent-reachable Cloudflare token can read or edit zone WAF rulesets (terraform/cloudflare README in declarative-config; credential blocker on bead pjp-815ae8ba). Token creation is an operator dashboard action.
3. Phase-ownership clobber risk: a cloudflare_ruleset in phase http_request_firewall_custom owns the WHOLE phase for the ardenone.com zone (one entrypoint ruleset per zone+phase). The live zone's dashboard-authored rules cannot be enumerated from here, so a first apply could silently destroy existing rules on a zone hosting sso/git/openbao — the same unverifiable-import hazard that killed the legacy terraform/cloudflare root (retired 2026-09-15, bead pjp-91185512).
4. Availability liability: the egress range drifts (plan risk table, MED). An unattended edge block rule on the shared host silently bricks the connector when Anthropic's ranges change.

Adoption recipe if the operator opts in:
1. Operator: create a least-privilege token (Zone > Zone WAF > Edit, ardenone.com only) and eyeball the zone's existing http_request_firewall_custom rules in the dashboard first — the ownership check that cannot be done from here.
2. New isolated edge root terraform/cloudflare-ardenone-edge/ in declarative-config (fleet pattern: cloudflare-pjp-edge, cloudflare-devimprint-edge; NOT the retired account-wide root), one cloudflare_ruleset, kind=zone, phase=http_request_firewall_custom, the block expression above.
3. Terraform CR in k8s/ardenone-manager/tofu-controller/ mirroring cloudflare-pjp-edge-terraform.yml; ExternalSecret sourcing the token from the ardenone-manager OpenBao prefix (value via pipe, never argv). Decide approvePlan deliberately: auto means the rule applies the moment the credential lands; omitted means a human approves the plan in the tofu UI (recommended for a shared host).
4. Before approving: capture the ibkr baseline (gate bead ytt-a7bb4bb4). After apply: non-Anthropic IP blocked at edge on /ytt paths, allowlisted IP reaches 401, ibkr well-known + basic call byte-identical, then re-check on the drift risk (plan risk table row already exists).

Revisit trigger: operator asks for it, or edge abuse from non-Anthropic IPs is observed despite the subject allowlist.

issue.close_reason: Root cause identified: NEEDLE backend descriptor for bead-rs has incorrect command syntax. The 'ready' operation uses ['ready', '--json', '--limit', '{limit}'] but bead-rs requires ['list', '--ready', '--json', '--limit', '{limit}']. Verified by running correct command which successfully returns open beads. Fix is to update NEEDLE/src/bead_store/backend.rs line 805 with the correct syntax.
issue.description:
## Diagnosis Phase

Based on investigation findings, pinpoint the exact configuration issue causing Pluck to miss open beads.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Identify the specific configuration setting causing the issue (exclude_labels, workspace path, or filter)
- Document the current vs expected configuration values
- Explain why the current setting excludes all 11 open beads
- Propose the specific fix needed

### Dependencies
Requires completion of investigation phase (bead ytt-roz) to understand the discovery mechanism.
issue.notes:
## Root Cause Identified

**Issue:** NEEDLE backend descriptor for bead-rs has incorrect command syntax for the 'ready' operation.

**Location:** /home/coding/NEEDLE/src/bead_store/backend.rs line 805

**Current configuration (WRONG):**
```rust
operations.insert(
    "ready".into(),
    operation(
        &["ready", "--json", "--limit", "{limit}"],  // bead-rs has no 'ready' subcommand
        None,
        Some(ParseShape::JsonLines),
    ),
);
```

**Expected configuration (CORRECT):**
```rust
operations.insert(
    "ready".into(),
    operation(
        &["list", "--ready", "--json", "--limit", "{limit}"],  // correct bead-rs syntax
        None,
        Some(ParseShape::JsonLines),
    ),
);
```

**Why this excludes all 11 open beads:**
When NEEDLE's Pluck strand tries to discover beads, it calls `bead ready --json --limit 999999`, which fails with 'error: unrecognized subcommand '\''ready'\'''. This command failure causes Pluck to return an empty candidate list, leading to the starvation alert even though 11 open beads exist in the workspace.

**Verification:**
Running the correct command `bead list --ready --json --limit 5` successfully returns open beads, confirming the syntax issue.

**Fix needed:**
Update the bead-rs backend descriptor in NEEDLE/src/bead_store/backend.rs to change the 'ready' operation from `["ready", "--json", "--limit", "{limit}"]` to `["list", "--ready", "--json", "--limit", "{limit}"]`.

Tested by: `bead list --ready --json --limit 5` returned 4 open beads successfully.
issue.title: Diagnose specific configuration issue preventing bead discovery

issue.close_reason:
Bounded download + Whisper resource guardrails implemented, tested, and pushed (HEAD 108ba6c on master, origin current).

Completed the partial work left by two 499-crashed attempts, then closed the remaining gaps:

1. Queued-work cap: YTT_MAX_PENDING_WHISPER_JOBS (default 16, fail-closed at 0, negatives rejected at startup) bounds the ASR backlog via new WhisperJobRegistry.active_count(). New caption-less jobs past the cap get the stable rate_limited error ("Whisper queue full (n/m)") before any quota spend; joining an in-flight job is always free; check ordering pinned (queue gate precedes the quota charge).
2. Duration: NoCaptionsError now carries the extract_info duration, so over-cap videos are refused too_long_for_asr at job creation — before a job is registered, a quota slot charged, or any audio downloaded; _do_download_audio re-enforces it as a download-time backstop when duration was unknown at creation (refusal happens before any bytes hit the wire).
3. Scratch cleanup: _sweep_video_scratch deletes {video_id}.* partial files after every job attempt, success or failure — a timed-out/aborted download previously leaked its partial (up to YTT_MAX_AUDIO_BYTES per failure) until restart; repeated failures could fill the scratch volume. Zombie-downloader safe (POSIX unlink semantics).
4. Cancellation: a cancelled job task releases its YTT_MAX_CONCURRENT_WHISPER slot, still sweeps its partial file, and the stale-running GC (timeout+TTL) recovers the registry entry; semaphore release on cancellation pinned by test.
5. Task-reference hardening: background job tasks are held by strong reference — the event loop keeps only weak ones, so an unpredictably GC'd task could strand a job as pending forever and permanently consume a queue slot (a leak the new cap couldn't see).

Stable errors used: rate_limited (queue full), too_long_for_asr (duration), asr_failed (timeouts, pre-existing). Config validation, defaults pin, and docs updated (docs/usage/configuration.md, README, CHANGELOG); deploy/ untouched — the default applies without a manifest change and the dispatch forbids writing to the declarative-config mirror repo.

14 new tests across tests/unit/test_whisper.py (duration backstop x4, scratch sweep x3, active_count x3, failed/cancelled-job hygiene + slot release), tests/unit/test_server.py (queue-full denial without quota spend, join-while-full, ordering, duration-at-creation), tests/unit/test_config.py (negative rejection, zero valid, defaults pin). Full unit suite: 791 passed, 1 skipped, 24 integration deselected. No new ruff findings vs HEAD~ (62 pre-existing on both).

The gate `close_verification` in workspace `/home/coding/ytt` failed with one identical fingerprint on 4 of the workspace's recent verification failures, across 4 distinct beads. The signal is statistical, not textual: when every failure in a workspace shares a fingerprint, no bead is at fault — the gate is.

- **Gate**: close_verification
- **Normalized output**: `close reason carries no verification evidence`
- **Fingerprint**: `ea603be160bd`
- **Window failures**: 4
- **Distinct beads affected**: 4

### Impact
This workspace is now **gate-degraded**: Pluck and Explore skip it for ordinary dispatch, and failures carrying this fingerprint no longer increment any bead's failure count. The workspace remains claimable — repairing the gate is verified by running it.

### Resolution
Fix the gate so a clean run passes, and the next successful verification in this workspace will clear the degradation, close this bead, and undo the failure penalties recorded while the window was degraded.

issue.description: Discovered while diagnosing why 0.2.6 (Authentik OAuth fix) was built but deployment.yml still pointed at 0.2.5: k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/ytt-build.yaml's resolve-version step clones github.com/jedarden/ytt (the read-only mirror, not Forgejo origin) and, when VERSION wasn't bumped by the developer, auto-commits+pushes the bump DIRECTLY to GitHub using a GH_TOKEN credential helper. This violates the fleet's Forgejo-primary/GitHub-read-only-mirror model (org CLAUDE.md, Git Hosting section) -- GitHub now has commits Forgejo doesn't, and Forgejo's server-side push-mirror can't cleanly propagate over that divergence on the next Forgejo push (non-fast-forward). Worked around this time by manually syncing Forgejo's VERSION file to match (ytt commit 7c7a435), which risks a mirror-sync failure on Forgejo's next push attempt, not touching data loss. Real fix: either have resolve-version clone/push against git.ardenone.com (Forgejo) instead of GitHub, or don't auto-bump/push in CI at all -- fail the build with a clear message if VERSION wasn't bumped, and require the version bump to happen in the same commit as the code change (matches k8s/CLAUDE.md Rule #8's stated convention already). Also worth checking whether other *-build.yaml WorkflowTemplates share this same clone-from-GitHub + push-to-GitHub pattern (armor-workflowtemplate.yml is cited as the template ytt-build.yaml mirrors).
issue.notes:
Investigation complete. ytt-build.yaml was already fixed on 2026-08-27 (commit df884e2d). The workflow now:
1. Clones from Forgejo (git.ardenone.com) instead of GitHub
2. Validates VERSION was changed instead of auto-bumping
3. Uses Forgejo token for read-only access only (no push path)

Other fleet *-build.yaml workflows checked:
- investment-research-mcp-build.yaml: Uses Forgejo ✓
- whofi-bench-build.yaml: Uses Forgejo ✓  
- commitgraph-compactor-build-workflowtemplate.yaml: Uses Forgejo ✓

pdftract-* workflows use GitHub but are for the public pdftract open-source project, not fleet infrastructure. They clone from GitHub tags and publish to public registries (npm, GitHub Releases) - this is intentional for a public OSS project.

No other fleet workflows have the problematic auto-bump + push pattern.

issue.notes:
## Pluck-Bead Mismatch Identified

### Summary
The `bead list --ready` command is NOT properly filtering out beads with the `deferred` label, causing Pluck to return beads that should be excluded.

### Current State
- **Total open beads**: 10 (not 13 - inventory is outdated)
- **Beads with excluded labels**: 1 (ytt-d9888685 has 'deferred')
- **Beads returned by `bead list --ready`**: 2

### The Mismatch
`bead list --ready` returns:
1. `ytt-d9888685` - Has **'deferred'** label (should be EXCLUDED but is RETURNED)
2. `ytt-a53c9acc` - Has 'verification-failed' label (not in default exclude list, correctly returned)

### Root Cause
The ready query is NOT respecting Pluck's default exclude_labels configuration ('deferred', 'human', 'blocked'). Bead `ytt-d9888685` should be filtered out because it has the 'deferred' label, but it's being returned as ready.

### Pluck Configuration (from docs)
- **Default exclude_labels**: ['deferred', 'human', 'blocked']
- **Expected behavior**: Beads with these labels should NOT be discoverable
- **Actual behavior**: Bead with 'deferred' label IS being returned

### Testing Performed
1. Verified Pluck configuration in docs/pluck-configuration.md
2. Checked all open beads and their labels
3. Tested `bead list --ready` output
4. Confirmed mismatch: deferred bead is returned when it should be filtered

### Impact
Pluck may attempt to process beads that were intentionally marked as deferred, violating the deferral intent.
issue.title: Identify Pluck-bead mismatch

issue.description:
docs/notes/auth.md requires DCR to be disabled for personal v1 ('DCR lets anyone register'; any future DCR must sit behind a pre-shared registration token), and docs/notes/http-endpoints.md shows /register mounted at both the bare and issuer-prefixed paths. No existing open bead covers this posture: the OAuth test beads target discovery/audience/path conformance (ytt-80a4da40) and the end-to-end authorization-code flow (ytt-9a7a9517), not registration. Add a regression test driving POST /register (both mount points) against the real ASGI app asserting open registration is rejected and no client credentials are issued, so a FastMCP upgrade or settings change cannot silently re-enable open DCR.

---
Priority: P2
Created by: weave strand
issue.notes:
Outcome: BLOCKED — the acceptance criterion ("asserting open registration is rejected and no client credentials are issued") is unimplementable as a passing test against the current app, because the premise describes a design that was deliberately retired. No files changed, nothing committed (nothing legitimate to commit); working tree untouched (other workers' in-flight edits present and left alone).

WHAT I VERIFIED (evidence):
1. Drove the real ASGI app (Starlette TestClient, unit-suite env/fake OIDC discovery): POST /register -> 201 with a client_id issued; POST /ytt/register -> 201 likewise. Registration response keys: client_id, client_id_issued_at, client_name, grant_types, redirect_uris, response_types, scope, token_endpoint_auth_method — NO client_secret (public client, token_endpoint_auth_method=none). GET /register -> 405. So "open registration is rejected" is factually not the shipped behavior: open registration IS the shipped behavior, by design.
2. fastmcp 3.4.2 (uv.lock) OAuthProxy has NO DCR-disable knob: register_client is an unconditional provider method; the constructor exposes no enable/disable-registration parameter. Disabling would mean hack-overriding register_client / dropping the route while ALSO removing registration_endpoint from the advertised AS metadata, or conformant clients break.
3. The shipped model — "DCR is open (required for OAuthProxy) but the fail-closed boundary is at authorization (Claude-only redirect allowlist) and tool calls (subject allowlist)" — is deliberately designed and already pinned by committed tests: tests/unit/test_auth.py::test_dcr_restricted_to_claude_redirect_uris (docstring verbatim: "DCR is open (required for OAuthProxy) but scoped to Claude's two redirect URIs"); tests/unit/test_oauth_conformance.py::TestDCRRestrictedToClaudeRedirects (closed bead ytt-80a4da40, commit f98d09a) drives POST /register asserting 201 and pins that a self-registered foreign/loopback redirect URI can never complete an authorization. The bead's claim that no existing test covers the registration posture is therefore incorrect as to ytt-80a4da40 — the uncovered surface is narrower (see below).
4. claude.ai itself registers via DCR against ytt: the 2026-07-16 production incident ("Couldn't register with YouTube Transcript's sign-in service") was exactly /register unreachable at the issuer-prefixed path, fixed by ADDING the second mount (ytt/auth.py docstring; tests/unit/test_auth.py route regression test — "old design had it disabled"). Re-disabling DCR breaks the product's only real client. The in-flight end-to-end suite of open bead ytt-9a7a9517 also drives DCR as working (201 -> client_id -> flow).
5. docs/notes/auth.md's "Dynamic Client Registration disabled for personal v1" is stale relative to the shipped model — it describes the pre-OIDCProxy design.

WHY NOT DONE AS SPECIFIED: (a) a passing rejection-asserting test cannot exist without contradicting the committed suite (self-contradictory CI; DoD step 3 could never pass); (b) making it pass by disabling DCR in code is a product-behavior change far outside this test-only bead's acceptance boundary, breaking the live connector and committed/in-flight tests — a decision for the operator, not a P2 test bead.

RECOMMENDED RESOLUTION (operator decision; either way reconcile docs/notes/auth.md):
(a) Re-scope test-only, pinning the ACTUAL fail-closed invariant: registration intentionally open (OAuthProxy + claude.ai requirement) but credential-free (no client_secret, public client) and authorization-gated (Claude-only redirect allowlist + subject allowlist). Genuinely uncovered today: bare /register mount never driven at HTTP level (only /ytt/register is), the no-client_secret property, 405 method discipline on both mounts, and the advertised registration_endpoint resolving to a live route.
(b) If the auth.md letter must be enforced: file a PRODUCT bead (not a test bead) — disable open DCR behind a pre-shared registration token, with a replacement client story for claude.ai (pre-registered client; note fastmcp 3.4.2 exposes enable_cimd), rewrites of test_auth.py::test_dcr_restricted_to_claude_redirect_uris and test_oauth_conformance.py TestDCRRestrictedToClaudeRedirects/register_client, coordination with in-flight ytt-9a7a9517, and auth.md/http-endpoints.md updates. Breaking change for the live connector; needs an explicit rollout decision.

detail.title: Decision: decline Cloudflare WAF IP allowlist for mcp.ardenone.com/ytt for now (optional defense-in-depth)

detail.reason: Decision recorded: the Cloudflare WAF/Access IP allowlist for mcp.ardenone.com/ytt is deliberately skipped for now, as optional defense-in-depth behind the fail-closed subject allowlist + audience-bound OAuth (the real authz, live). Access is the wrong product (would challenge the unattended backend); a path-scoped WAF custom rule is the right shape and the recipe for adopting it is in the bead body. Not adopted because: plan.md gates it to an explicit human choice that hasn't been made; no agent-reachable Cloudflare token can read/edit zone WAF rulesets (pjp-815ae8ba credential blocker); the zone-wide http_request_firewall_custom phase ownership risks clobbering unverifiable dashboard rules on a shared zone (the hazard that retired the legacy terraform/cloudflare root); and the drifting Anthropic egress range makes an unattended edge block a standing availability liability. Revisit on operator request or observed edge abuse.

Resolved via the second path the task offered: the WAF/Access IP allowlist for mcp.ardenone.com/ytt is deliberately skipped as optional defense-in-depth, and the decision is now formally recorded.

What was done:
- Created and closed decision bead ytt-761fb151 (unique-ref ytt:cloudflare-waf-ip-allowlist-decision) recording the decline with full rationale and an adoption recipe: path-scoped WAF custom rule (http.host eq "mcp.ardenone.com" and (starts_with(uri.path,"/ytt") or ends_with(uri.path,"/ytt")) and not ip.src in {160.79.104.0/21 2607:6bc0::/48}) → block, which leaves every /ibkr path untouched; isolated terraform/cloudflare-ardenone-edge root per the pjp/devimprint-edge fleet pattern; ibkr regression gate before/after.
- Corrected docs/notes/auth.md (commit e5d16b1): the premise "must live at Cloudflare Access/WAF" was the source of the gap — Access is the wrong product (an identity gate that would challenge Anthropic's unattended backend), the control is optional defense-in-depth behind the fail-closed subject allowlist, and the decision bead is now referenced from the doc.

Why not author the rule now: plan.md gates it to an explicit human choice that hasn't been made; no agent-reachable Cloudflare token can read/edit zone WAF rulesets (credential blocker pjp-815ae8ba); a cloudflare_ruleset in phase http_request_firewall_custom owns the entire phase for the ardenone.com zone and live dashboard rules are unverifiable from here, so a first apply could clobber existing rules on the zone hosting sso/git/openbao — the same unverifiable-import hazard that retired the legacy terraform/cloudflare root (pjp-91185512, 2026-09-15); and the drifting Anthropic egress range makes an unattended edge block a standing availability liability for an optional control.

Scratch cleanup: _sweep_video_scratch deletes {video_id}.* partial files after every job attempt, success or failure — a timed-out/aborted download previously leaked its partial (up to YTT_MAX_AUDIO_BYTES per failure) until restart; repeated failures could fill the scratch volume. Zombie-downloader safe (POSIX unlink semantics).
4. Cancellation: a cancelled job task releases its YTT_MAX_CONCURRENT_WHISPER slot, still sweeps its partial file, and the stale-running GC (timeout+TTL) recovers the registry entry; semaphore release on cancellation pinned by test.
5. Task-reference hardening: background job tasks are held by strong reference — the event loop keeps only weak ones, so an unpredictably GC'd task could strand a job as pending forever and permanently consume a queue slot (a leak the new cap couldn't see).
